question:
(i) Explain the principle of a velocity selector using mutually perpendicular electric and magnetic fields. Derive the condition for a charged particle to pass undeflected.
(ii) In a velocity selector, $E=4.5\times10^4\text{ V m}^{-1}$ and $B=0.30\text{ T}$. Calculate the speed of particles that pass through without deflection.

options.A: In a velocity selector the forces add, so $qE+qvB=0$ and $v=\dfrac{B}{E}=6.7\times10^{-6}\,\text{m s}^{-1}$.
options.B: With $\vec E$, $\vec B$ and $\vec v$ mutually perpendicular, a particle is undeflected when electric and magnetic forces are equal and opposite: $qE=qvB$. Hence $v=\dfrac{E}{B}=\dfrac{4.5\times10^4}{0.30}=1.5\times10^5\,\text{m s}^{-1}$.
options.C: Only particles with $v=EB=1.35\times10^4\,\text{m s}^{-1}$ are undeflected.
options.D: The selector condition is $qE=qB/v$, so $v=\dfrac{B}{E}=6.7\times10^{-6}\,\text{m s}^{-1}$.
